character_sheet: The King is the three-headed flying boss the Queen answers to, on the same family of rig as hers: a body with a chest, back plates and six ridge spines, three four-segment necks each ending in a maned, spiked, jawed and toothed head, two clawed legs of thigh, upper leg, lower leg and foot with three double claws and a rear claw each, two enormous ten-panel wings, and a seven-segment tail ending in two tip pieces and a spike (ModelTheKing.createBodyLayer, ModelTheKing.java:309-940). It has 7000 HP, 350 attack and 21 armour (MobStats.THE_KING, createAttributes TheKing.java:232-240), a red boss bar (:118-119), no physics and no gravity (:155-157) — it flies from spawn — and five manual hitbox parts that ride the root: body 5x5, head 3x3, wingL and wingR 5x2, tail 3x3 (:167-172, :463-467; the head takes full damage, the body half, the rest a quarter plus one, :411-419). Its primary goal (KingPrimaryGoal, aiStepPrimary :735-905) wanders it around its home and, on a 1-in-5 pass (1-in-3 when hurt or enraged), takes its revenge target or the nearest suitable thing in an 80x64x80 scan, raises the attacking flag and flies to just above it (:776-830); within 30 blocks it stomps — a 15-block damage ring on a 1-in-2 roll and the bite (:843-848) — and rings the ground 20 blocks ahead on a 1-in-3 (:853-857); beyond 30, by a 1-in-3 choice, it fires a fireball, a lightning bolt or an ice ball when its head is aimed, ten, five and eight to a stream (:863-881); enraged (the end game's phase 2) it spews purple power (:888-902). Its damage doubles with each quarter of health lost (:496-507), it heals back to 2000 while it has taken fewer than ten player hits (:603-611), takes clamped damage (:972-999), and calls up its invisible gaze-tracking head sidecar (:808-815). The end game freezes the nearest player for a dialogue and a countdown before the enraged phase (aiStepEndGameDialogue :638-693). Its wings sound every 30 ticks (:484-490). It has no natural spawn (it is summoned, or grown from the Prince Adult after 288000 tame ticks). Read it as the Queen's mate: a vast slow wing-beat, three heads snaking on their own rhythms, the tail sweeping, and a fury of claws, legs and jaws when it attacks.
size_notes: Drawn at x2.1 of the rig, a quarter of that while PlayNicely (TheKingRenderer.java:52, applied :66-73; shadow 1.9 x 2.1) on a 2048x2048 sheet (ModelTheKing.java:940); 22 x 24 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:214-216; 5.5 x 6 while PlayNicely, BOSS-017). The five manual part hitboxes are placed from the root position, not from the pose (TheKing.java:463-467) — until the bone-synced profile lands, the heads', wings' and tail's hit surfaces do not move with your keys. The necks, wings, legs and tail are chains the code positions segment by segment — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: wings

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.08 = 0.251 rad (14 deg) at 0.26 rad/tick; attacking: pi x 0.19 = 0.597 rad (34 deg) at 0.56 rad/tick; the base takes half the wave, segments 2 to 4 the full wave an eighth of a period apart, then segments 5, 6, 7, the tip and the spike each add half of segment 4's wave; every segment placed at the end of the one before (54 / 42 / 41 / 34 / 34 / 40 / 43 / 58 units)

behaviour: Every rhythm is time-driven and switched by the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (TheKing.java:104, raised at :820 with a target and at :866-872 while aiming a stream, cleared at :878); nothing reads the walking speed, the walk position or the look angles — the King has no gait and its heads do not follow the look.

The two wings beat 27 degrees at 0.35 rad/tick (an 18-tick beat) at rest and 38 degrees at 0.75 attacking, the elbow spars 5/3 and the tips 7/3 of that, the spread panels fanned ±15 degrees from the elbow, each spar placed at the end of the one before (ModelTheKing.java:949-993).

Calm, the claws and legs hold their rests; attacking, the fourteen claws flex 45 degrees at 0.75 rad/tick (:995-1012) and the legs kick alternately 81 degrees at 0.6 — a quarter of it on the thighs, a half on the lower legs and feet (:1014-1043). The tail sweeps in a travelling wave that curls harder toward the spike — 14 degrees at 0.26 rad/tick at rest, 34 at 0.56 attacking (:1045-1082).

The three heads snake on their own sines, each head on a different yaw, pitch and jaw rate (left 0.17 / 0.13 / 0.45, centre 0.13 / 0.08 / 0.65, right 0.19 / 0.12 / 0.55 calm; 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.85, 0.28 / 0.19 / 0.75, 0.32 / 0.21 / 0.95 attacking), 14 and 18 degrees at rest and 45 attacking, the outer heads clamped never to cross the centre one; each four-segment neck takes an eighth, a quarter, 0.38 and a half of the head's angles and is placed link by link (:1084-1122, :1125-1532).

The stomp rings (doJumpDamage, TheKing.java:843-857), the bite (doHurtTarget :938-957), the fireball, lightning and ice streams (:863-875) and the purple-power spew (:888-902) are rolled by aiStepPrimary; the five manual part hitboxes are placed from the root each tick (:463-467) — none of these are animation events.

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelTheKing row (geckolib_migration_design.md:453): 'Preserve current topology and sizes as the first candidate: Body1 [5,5] @0.5; CHead1/LHead1/RHead1 [3,3] @1; Lwing1/Rwing1 [5,2] @0.25; Tail1/Tail4/Tail7 [3,3] @0.25; upper/lower legs/feet [2.5,6] @0.5'. Body1, CHead1, LHead1, RHead1, Lwing1, Rwing1, Tail1, Tail4 and Tail7 resolve as written. 'upper/lower legs/feet' is not a bone name: taken as LUpperLeg / LLowerLeg / LFoot and RUpperLeg / RLowerLeg / RFoot (ModelTheKing.createBodyLayer); the thighs LThigh / RThigh, which the code poses with the upper legs (:1019, :1032), are not named by the row and stay visual until the owner says otherwise. The sizes are today's five manual OreSpawnPartEntity parts (TheKing.java:167-172: body 5x5, head 3x3, wingL / wingR 5x2, tail 3x3), which the row keeps live until the profile passes and replaces them atomically; the row also retains the invisible king_head sidecar.
formulas: `ModelTheKing.poseFrom` (ModelTheKing.java:973-1152 with its three head helpers; orig ModelTheKing.java:873-1149 in `render` (func_78088_a, :856-1151; func_78087_a at :1159-1161 is a bare super call), the port's WING_SPEED 1.0 where orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:492 passes `new ModelTheKing(0.65f)` - the port's model is what the hook transcribes): every rhythm switches on the attacking flag. The wing angle is the cosine of the age in ticks times 0.75 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.21 while attacking, else the cosine of the age times 0.35 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.15: the left wing's root and second part roll by it, the third and fourth by five thirds of it, the fifth and sixth by seven thirds; the third's pivot follows the root 84 units along the cosine (x) and sine (y) of the root's roll and the fifth's the third by 184 along the third's; the seventh to tenth parts ride the third's place, the seventh and eighth at 0.261 plus the third's roll and the ninth and tenth at minus 0.261 plus it; the right wing mirrors it (the negatives, the follows the other way). The thirteen claw parts flex, attacking, by the cosine of the age times 0.75 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.25 (else 0) around their rests -0.925, 0.384 and 0.645. The legs swing, attacking, by the cosine of the age times 0.6 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.45 (else 0): a quarter of it on the thigh and upper leg around 0.785, half on the lower leg and foot around -0.628, the lower leg placed 50 units down the upper leg's pitch and the seven claws of each foot 66 units down the lower leg's (at -0.1 and 0.15 of pitch). The tail's eight rings yaw on the cosine of the age times the tail speed times the wing speed - 0.56 attacking, 0.26 at rest - times pi, times the amplitude (0.19 / 0.08), lagging a quarter turn per ring and each placed 54 (a unit to the left), 42, 41, 34, 34, 40, 43 and 58 units from the ring before along the cosine (z) and sine (x) of its yaw; the two rear ridges copy the first ring's yaw and the sixth ridge the seventh ring's. The three heads sweep, attacking, by the sine of the age times 0.3 (the left), 0.28 (the centre) and 0.32 (the right) times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.25 sideways and the sine of the age times 0.2 / 0.19 / 0.21 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.25 up and down, the jaws by the sine of the age times 0.85 / 0.75 / 0.95 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.12 over 0.5; at rest the sine of the age times 0.17 / 0.13 / 0.19 times the wing speed, times pi, times 0.08 sideways, 0.13 / 0.08 / 0.12 times pi times 0.1 up and down, and the jaws 0.45 / 0.65 / 0.55 times pi times 0.04 over 0.25 - each jaw adding its head's pitch; the side heads are clamped to the centre head's sweep; each head's four neck rings yaw and pitch at 0.125, 0.25, 0.38 and 0.5 of it, following one another by 20, 36, 36 and 36 units first sideways, then foreshortened and lifted by the pitch chain, the head group (three head parts, the mane, two eyes, two nose spikes) riding the fourth ring by 36 units and the jaw group (three jaws, four teeth) by 37 and 14 more along the head's pitch. The walk position and speed play no part. The ten wing membranes are drawn a second time translucent at the 0.75 / 0.75 / 0.75 / 0.55 tint (ModelTheKing.WING_MEMBRANE_RENDER_TYPE / WING_MEMBRANE_COLOR; TEST-018: the descriptor's second pass, the seam's SecondPassLayer). The GeckoLib hook is the same (TheKingGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
